text:
incident-bot: P99 latency alert: streaming.websocket.raptor-prod > 2.5s for last 3m. P95 also drifting. https://grafana.redwood.local/d/streaming
alice.sre: I'm oncall, taking this — joining bridge.
ben.runtime: saw spike right after kernel rollout v2.1.3 at 02:12 UTC, possible KV cache churn.
charlie.mlinfra: streaming stalls look like tail requests hitting eviction; prefix cache miss rate jumped.
dana.support: customer-impact check: 4 open chat tickets from EU customers mentioning stalls.
alice.sre: running quick p95/p99 query now:
```
SELECT quantile(0.95, latency) AS p95, quantile(0.99, latency) AS p99
FROM streaming_requests
WHERE env='prod' AND region='eu-west' AND timestamp > now() - interval '5 minutes'
GROUP BY minute
```
alice.sre: quick results: p95 ~420ms -> 1.2s, p99 ~620ms -> 3.4s; sharp inflection at 02:11:30 UTC correlating with kvcache eviction spikes.
ben.runtime: KV metrics check: `curl -s http://kvcache-metrics.local/metrics | grep hit_rate`
ops-bot: KV cache hit_rate dropped from 0.98 -> 0.72 at 02:11:45 UTC (annotated).
charlie.mlinfra: canary rollback of kernel would take ~8m; alternative: shift streaming routing to dedicated low-latency pool for eu-west.
alice.sre: applied temporary routing override to dedicated-pool-eu-west. Increasing trace sampling for streaming service.
alice.sre: mitigation check in 30s — p99 dropped to ~1.1s after routing change, p95 ~350ms. Some intermittent stalls persist.
ben.runtime: applied short-term config: reduce batching window from 20ms -> 5ms on streaming path to prioritize latency.
charlie.mlinfra: starting canary rollback on 2 hosts to validate kernel hypothesis.
dana.support: posting brief update to affected customers and support queue.
alice.sre: will keep page open for 20m observation window, then decide rollback or full routing.
incident-bot: Note: p99 spike detected; temporary routing + batching changes applied; canary rollback in progress.
